overview: White plays 3.b4 against the fianchettoed Black set-up, aiming for a Reti-style double fianchetto with Bb2 and Bg2 and queenside expansion with a4 and b5. Black usually plays 3...Bg7 4.Bb2 O-O and counters in the centre with ...d6 and ...e5 or ...c5. The game is manoeuvring, with White trying to use the long diagonal.

white_ideas.idea: Double fianchetto with Bb2 and Bg2 and aim at the long diagonal
Expand on the queenside with a4, b5 and c4

black_ideas.idea: Mirror with ...Bg7 and ...O-O, then play ...d6 and ...e5
Strike with ...c5 to challenge the b4 pawn

typical_structures.structure: Reti-style fianchetto set-up with queenside space for White

character.notes: The play is mostly manoeuvring around the long diagonal and the b4 pawn, not forcing.

gambit.notes: The b4 pawn can be challenged by ...c5, but ...Nxb... does not win it by force and nothing is offered at the root.

soundness.notes: A well-known sound set-up with the b4 advance.

structure.notes: Pawn centres are undecided and both players keep options open.

approach.notes: A named, respectable Reti idea, but it is a specific plan rather than a set-up you can play against everything.

level.notes: The plans are positional, with limited memorisation.

character.reason: Manoeuvring play on both wings without forced lines.

gambit.reason: The b4 pawn is not a planned sacrifice.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre undecided.

approach.reason: A named Reti plan, but it is aimed at the symmetrical g6 defence only.

plans.reason: White develops both bishops on the long diagonals and expands on the queenside.
